overview: Jenny Graham and Matt Rice discussed Design Option B for the Medford High School building project, focusing on a renovation-and-addition model that reuses the existing structure. The session highlighted the environmental benefits of retaining embodied carbon and the necessity of adding 120,000 square feet to meet modern educational requirements.

items.title: Comparison of Design Options A and B
items.summary: Jenny Graham and Matt Rice contrasted Design Option A's basic repairs with Option B's strategy of keeping the existing frame while reimagining internal spaces to meet the district's educational plan.

items.title: Embodied Carbon and Environmental Impact
items.summary: Matt Rice explained that Option B prioritizes 'embodied carbon' by salvaging the energy-intensive concrete used in the original 1970 construction to reduce the project's overall carbon footprint.

items.title: Vertical Expansion and Site Preservation
items.summary: The proposed design preserves Edgerly Field and existing parking by adding two stories on top of the current B and D wings to accommodate 120,000 square feet of additional space.

items.title: Educational Programming and Facility Needs
items.summary: Graham detailed how the expansion would right-size Career and Technical Education and special education spaces while co-locating early childhood programs and the Curtis Tufts school on the main campus.
